utterances.speaker: spk_1
utterances.text: Kestrelmoor Clinics, this is Priya.

utterances.speaker: spk_2
utterances.text: Hi Priya, it's Sam from Vantrellis. I saw your team finished the Harlow Street job last week. How did that land?

utterances.speaker: spk_1
utterances.text: Ha, it was a sprint, but we got there. Thanks for asking.

utterances.speaker: spk_2
utterances.text: Today I'll walk you through how we work and then show you the product.

utterances.speaker: spk_1
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: spk_2
utterances.text: Walk me through what filling last-minute cancellations looks like today?

utterances.speaker: spk_1
utterances.text: Honestly it's a spreadsheet. Our front desk lead spends two or three hours a day on the phone on it.

utterances.speaker: spk_2
utterances.text: What makes that the hardest part?

utterances.speaker: spk_1
utterances.text: Things change after it's done. Last time, we had eleven empty slots last Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: spk_2
utterances.text: And when that happens, what does it look like for you personally?

utterances.speaker: spk_1
utterances.text: I'm the one on the phone apologizing. It's the part of the job I hate.

utterances.speaker: spk_2
utterances.text: If nothing changes over the next six months, what does that cost you?

utterances.speaker: spk_1
utterances.text: Honestly? Roughly four thousand dollars a week in empty chairs. And people are tired of it.

utterances.speaker: spk_2
utterances.text: What are you hoping a new tool would do for you?

utterances.speaker: spk_1
utterances.text: Just make it easier, really.

utterances.speaker: spk_2
utterances.text: Okay, that makes sense.

utterances.speaker: spk_1
utterances.text: Yeah.

utterances.speaker: spk_2
utterances.text: You said our front desk lead spends two or three hours a day on the phone on filling last-minute cancellations. With us, open slots go out to the waitlist by text automatically. That's the part that would have caught it when we had eleven empty slots last Tuesday.

utterances.speaker: spk_1
utterances.text: Okay. What does something like that cost?

utterances.speaker: spk_2
utterances.text: It's twenty-four thousand dollars a year.

utterances.speaker: spk_1
utterances.text: That's steep for us.

utterances.speaker: spk_2
utterances.text: I hear you. I could probably do fifteen percent off if that helps.

utterances.speaker: spk_1
utterances.text: Maybe. I'd have to think about it.

utterances.speaker: spk_2
utterances.text: Who else weighs in on a decision like this, and how have you bought software like this before?

utterances.speaker: spk_1
utterances.text: I'd bring in Casey, our owner. Casey signs anything over ten thousand. Last time it took about a month with a trial first.

utterances.speaker: spk_2
utterances.text: So a trial, then Casey, about a month. Is there a date you'd want this live by?

utterances.speaker: spk_1
utterances.text: Before the busy season, so November.

utterances.speaker: spk_2
utterances.text: Does what you've seen so far make sense for your team?

utterances.speaker: spk_1
utterances.text: Can you just send me some info and I'll look it over?

utterances.speaker: spk_2
utterances.text: Well, honestly, the info won't show you much. We're actually cheaper than most of the market.

utterances.speaker: spk_1
utterances.text: Okay. Send it anyway.

utterances.speaker: spk_2
utterances.text: Can we put thirty minutes on the calendar with Casey for Thursday at ten, so you both see it running with your tools?

utterances.speaker: spk_1
utterances.text: Thursday at ten works. I'll forward the invite to Casey.

utterances.speaker: spk_2
utterances.text: Thanks Priya, really appreciate the time.

utterances.speaker: spk_1
utterances.text: Thanks, bye.
